title: Stride-based decoding loop
statement: Let $A$ be a register program with $m$ registers and $d$ oracle queries, with input $y$, and let $r_{\mathrm{ptr}},r_{\mathrm{base}},r_{\mathrm{acc}},r_{\mathrm{tmp}}$ be pairwise distinct registers. Suppose the instructions at labels $\mathrm{test},\mathrm{downs}(i),\mathrm{read},\mathrm{copy}(b),\mathrm{bump}(b),\mathrm{clear}(b),\mathrm{scale}(b),\mathrm{take}(b),\mathrm{incs}(b,i),\mathrm{add}(b)$ have the specified loop form: test compares pointer with base; each of the first $\mathrm{stride}$ down labels decrements the pointer and leads to read; read queries oracle $j$ on the whole input with the pointer value; copy compares temporary with accumulator and branches to clear or bump; bump increments temporary and returns to copy; clear resets the accumulator; scale tests temporary for zero; take decrements it; the first two increment labels increment the accumulator and lead back to scale; and add either increments the accumulator and returns to test or tests temporary for zero and returns to test. Assume these instruction equations hold with the stated continuations, including that the decrement chain has length $\mathrm{stride}$, the increment chain has length two, and $\mathrm{stride}>0$. Let $w$ be a bit string and $k\leq |w|$. Suppose every suffix binary value of $w$ is at most $B$, all initial registers are at most $B$, the pointer is initially the base value plus $\mathrm{stride}\,k$, the accumulator is initially the binary value of the suffix of $w$ beginning at $k$, and the temporary register is zero. Also suppose that for every $i<|w|$, the oracle answer on the pair encoding of $y$ and the binary representation of the base value plus $\mathrm{stride}\,i$ equals bit $i$ of $w$. Then there is a final register assignment, still bounded by $B$, with pointer equal to its initial base value, accumulator equal to the binary value of $w$, and temporary register zero; every other register is unchanged. The program has a finite guarded execution from test to done, where every earlier configuration satisfies the program's safety condition and register bound.
